Aide à l’emploi : la bibliothèque Atwate: Job search help: Atwater Library meets the needs of English-speaking newcomers
Contrer les embûches à l'emploi pour les: Removing barriers to employment for asylum seekers in libraries
Liz et Maya travaillent à la bibliothèqu: Liz and Maya work at Atwater Library and offer a job search assistance service. One of the obstacles to getting help is a lack of resources, but also a lack of access to a computer or even a printer. Photo: Anais Elboujdaini
Depuis octobre, la Bibliothèque Atwater: Since October, Atwater Library has offered volunteer-led job search services. The CELI Career Fair is a casual event where migrants, both asylum seekers and refugees, can get advice on finding work in an intimate setting. Most of them express themselves better in English, so help can be offered to them in that language.
Un autre objectif du centre de carrière:
Another goal of the career centre? “It’s an accessible place with few barriers to participation, where people can come for help finding a job, improving their job skills or simply having someone to talk to about their job search,” says Maya Garfinkel, the project coordinator at Atwater Library.

The sessions take place on the second floor of the building, which was built in 1920, with all the wood panelling and huge arched windows that implies. The library has been designated a “National Historic Site of Canada,” and the meetings take place on church pews in a vast room.
Pour Maya, gérer les attentes est import: For Maya, managing expectations is important: “We really try to meet people where they are by providing resources as non-professional employment advisers.”
Deux hommes, tout sourire, disent au rev: Two men, all smiles, say goodbye to Maya. They came for some advice on their job search, but have to hurry to make it to the local food bank on time. “That’s really the reality they have to deal with,” she says.
Idriss est un demandeur d’asile qui a en: Idriss is an asylum seeker who has had his work permit for several weeks. Still, he is finding it hard to land a job. He spoke with La Converse in a café after a job search assistance session. Photo: Anais Elboujdaini
En raison de sa proximité avec le YMCA,: Because it is close to the YMCA, which houses asylum seekers, the library is often used by them, among other things for its computers, for a minimal fee. At Atwater Library, most of the “employees” are actually volunteers. They therefore often found themselves in a particular situation they were not prepared for, says Liz Perrin, who is in charge of digital literacy.
Ceux-ci ont en effet noté une demande co: They noticed a constant demand for résumé printing. “Someone comes in and asks the volunteer, ‘I just need to print my résumé,’ and the volunteer is really only equipped to say, ‘OK, email it to me or let me help you log in to your email,’” says Ms. Perrin.
Or, assez rapidement dans ce genre de co: But quite quickly in this kind of conversation, the volunteer realizes that the person needs help creating a résumé. “Access to a printer is great, but the résumé doesn’t even exist yet. So I think that was a big driver to do something to meet that need,” she says.
Idriss* a longtemps travaillé en Maurita: Idriss* worked for a long time in Mauritania for a well-known organization, where he did cleaning and maintenance. “In my country, slavery still exists,” he says, barely above a whisper. The man in his thirties was therefore never able to go to school.
Bien que le pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest ai: Although the West African country abolished hereditary slavery in 1981, modern slavery persists there. In 2023, <l1>Mauritania ranked third on the sordid global podium of countries where modern slavery is most prevalent</l1>.
Idriss s’exprime en français seulement,: Idriss speaks only French, but he gets the help he needs to start his job search at the Atwater Library fair, even though its target audience is English-speaking asylum seekers. Although he has his work permit, he faces a major challenge: he can neither read nor write. The job fair therefore gives him a first access to resources. “I want to work, but for now I haven’t found anything yet. It’s hard because sometimes they give me forms to fill out, and it’s complicated…” he says, trailing off.
« C’est un ami sénégalais qui m’en a par: “A Senegalese friend told me about it at the YMCA,” adds the man who has since found an apartment.
Si Idriss est francophone, c’est loin d’: While Idriss is francophone, that is far from the case for all the visitors to the job fair. “We are bilingual, even multilingual,” Liz explains. She says the project is “planting seeds around the city,” as it tries to build bridges between several organizations such as the YMCA, but also an organization in Sherbrooke that gives English literacy lessons.
La bibliothèque Atwater de MontréalPhoto: Atwater Library in Montréal. Photo: Anais Elboujdaini
La Bibliothèque d’Atwater a été fondée e: Atwater Library was founded in 1828. Today, it operates independently from the rest of the City of Montréal’s municipal library network. It differs in many respects, partly because, as mentioned, most of its employees are not actually employees: volunteers keep the place running. At the heart of the library’s mission are continuing education courses and digital literacy. It is no surprise that the job assistance program for newcomers was born there.
Si ce programme répond à un besoin crian: While this program answers a pressing need in the community that uses the library, Atwater Library is not the only one offering help to asylum seekers and refugees. The Vancouver Public Library (VPL) has a page of links for refugees and asylum seekers on its website.
« Quand nous avons accueilli des réfugié: “When we welcomed Ukrainian refugees, we put housing assistance resources in place,” says Alicia Cheng, information lead at the VPL. “We direct them to the relevant resources. But other questions come up. For immigrants, we let them know about immigration resources. Then at some point, some people are looking for more specific things, so we help them as best we can.”
Plus près de Montréal, les <l1>bibliothè: Closer to Montréal, <l1>New York’s libraries</l1> support asylum seekers. In 2023, during the presentation of the Big Apple’s municipal budget, the library system’s chief executive stressed <l2>the importance of maintaining the institution’s budget because of its role</l2> in integrating asylum seekers.
<l1>Des recherches montrent d’ailleurs l: <l1>Research also shows the crucial role of public libraries in the integration of migrants</l1>: “Migrants also seek free access to the internet and digital resources. [...] From the migrants’ perspective, isolation, illiteracy and prejudice or a lack of knowledge about the library are highlighted [as barriers].”
Rien ne laissait présager que le program: Nothing suggested that the program could give volunteers a chance to share their experience and reassure newcomers, who are often filled with apprehension.
« Parfois, je vois deux personnes en tra: “Sometimes I see two people chatting and I think they’re two volunteers who already know each other, but one of them is a client, and they’ve just met,” says Liz, pleasantly surprised.
C’est le soutien mutuel entre bénévoles: It is the mutual support between volunteers and participants that makes this kind of exchange unique, because everyone is on an equal footing. “We try to be really good at managing expectations, without ever positioning ourselves as experts,” she says.
Ils viennent de l’Iran, de l’Algérie, du: That day, they come from Iran, Algeria, Kenya, Mauritania and Chad. Not all of them speak English, but those who get by better in that language are served without any problem.
En raison des partenariats, notamment av: Thanks to partnerships, notably with the Refugee Centre, some volunteers are refugees themselves and can share their experience with newcomers who have everything to discover.
« Je pense que les personnes qui ont véc: “I think people who have lived this experience or who know people who have are really eager to help. It’s a very powerful motivator,” says the woman, who has witnessed many situations of great vulnerability between participants and volunteers.
« Même si ce n’est pas la même expérienc: “Even if it’s not the same experience, the emotions are there. It makes creating an email account, for example, much more intimate and warm, even if it’s a relatively mundane thing.”
« Lorsqu’un bénévole est capable de mont: “When a volunteer is able to show that vulnerability, to go beyond the technical aspects and reach out to someone, it makes all the difference, and it’s perhaps something harder to get in a larger, more bureaucratic world of social services,” she concludes.
Une bénévole originaire du Kenya attend: A volunteer from Kenya waits to greet someone she can help. In the meantime, she is looking for a job herself. She knows that her high-level experience in her country of origin will probably not be recognized here. And she doesn’t yet speak the language, having arrived in Quebec in December.
Accueillie comme réfugiée, elle se fait:
Welcomed as a refugee, she makes it her duty to help others by volunteering. When asked whether she plans to leave Quebec, she frowns and exclaims that she loves Montréal. “Me, I want to settle here and learn French,” she says. “Maybe it’s easier to go to Ontario, but I think I could be happy here,” she adds.

Quebec’s French Language Commissioner, Benoît Dubreuil, proposed in a report published on February 14 that asylum seekers who do not speak French be redirected to an English-speaking province. He suggests <l1>“directing people who claim asylum to provinces whose main language they know” in order to avoid the costs of language instruction through French-language integration courses.</l1>
De son côté, Idriss cherche toujours un: As for Idriss, he is still looking for a job. Phone in hand, he has been criss-crossing the city for two months to sort out every problem he runs into: finding housing, winter clothes, a job. The Atwater job fair is one small step to help him climb the staircase of his integration.
« Ici, il y a beaucoup de liberté et bea: “Here, there is a lot of freedom and a lot of possibilities,” he concludes.
